title: The Log Cabinet
topic: File handling: text, CSV and JSON files
briefing: Head office sends orders as files and wants production logs back as files. There's a text file of orders, a CSV spreadsheet of board test results, and a JSON file of specs. Read them all, then write a proper production log. Paperwork, but important paperwork!
hints: with open("orders.txt") as f: lets you read the file with f.read(). .splitlines() turns the text into a list of lines. Open with "w" to write (it replaces the file) and "a" to append (it adds to the end).
json.load(f) turns a JSON file into a dict. csv.DictReader(f) gives one dict per row, so wrap it in list(). os.path.exists("name") checks whether a file exists.

with open("orders.txt") as f: orders = f.read().splitlines() / with open("specs.json") as f: specs = json.load(f) then socket = specs["socket"] / with open("boards.csv") as f: rows = list(csv.DictReader(f)) / passed = [r["serial"] for r in rows if r["status"] == "PASS"] / write: with open("production.log", "w") as f: for o in orders: f.write(f"BUILT {o}\n") / then open with "a" and write "SHIFT END\n"
bonus: Use os.listdir() to print every file in the folder, and os.remove() to delete production.log. Then check os.path.exists again.
